extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator and general early-18th-century literate public (coffee-house readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial/polemical essays for The Spectator: short moral and cultural commentaries aimed at correcting social vices, prescribing manners, and critiquing arts (music/opera) for a broad public readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address causes of vanity, not merely fashion
rubrics_metrics.description: “it is not my Intention to sink the Dignity of this my Paper with Reflections upon Red-heels or Top-knots, but rather to enter into the Passions of Mankind, and to correct those depraved Sentiments that give Birth to all those little Extravagancies which appear in their outward Dress and Behaviour.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus criticism on the underlying dispositions (vanity, passions, 'depraved Sentiments') that produce fashionable excesses, rather than attacking particular ornaments or transient fashions themselves. The editor proposes remedying root causes so the superficial 'Blossoms' fall of themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat foppish ornaments as indications of vice
rubrics_metrics.description: “Foppish and fantastick Ornaments are only Indications of Vice, not criminal in themselves. Extinguish Vanity in the Mind, and you naturally retrench the little Superfluities of Garniture and Equipage.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging dress and show, view them as symptoms pointing to moral shortcomings; remedial attention should be directed at reforming sentiments (vanity) rather than criminalizing individual articles of dress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose limited censorship of small fashions (editorial office idea)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author contemplates creating an officer entituled 'The Censor of small Wares' to allot a day weekly for executing such oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a policy option: establish a regular, small-scale editorial function to call out and correct recurring petty extravagances of dress and behaviour, acting analogously to a surgeon treating local symptoms while the editor treats constitutional causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish private scandal or single-person lampoons
rubrics_metrics.description: “it is not my Design to be a Publisher of Intreagues and Cuckoldoms... If I attack the Vicious, I shall only set upon them in a Body: and will not be provoked by the worst Usage that I can receive from others, to make an Example of any particular Criminal.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid printing private calumny or naming individuals; expose and criticize vices as types or species (collective wrongs), not as particulars to be shamed or defamed in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep clear of party politics; avoid partisan exacerbation
rubrics_metrics.description: “as I am very sensible my Paper would lose its whole Effect, should it run into the Outrages of a Party, I shall take Care to keep clear of every thing which looks that Way... I shall apply my self to it with my utmost Endeavours; but will never let my Heart reproach me with having done any thing towards encreasing those Feuds and Animosities that extinguish Religion, deface Government, and make a Nation miserable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain neutrality and avoid taking sides in party disputes; the paper's aim is to soothe inflammations and allay public ferments rather than inflame partisan conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial acceptance: supply innocent diversion and publish general-interest materials
rubrics_metrics.description: “if he has started any Hint which he is not able to pursue... if he has discovered any epidemical Vice which has escaped my Observation, or has heard of any uncommon Virtue which he would desire to publish; in short, if he has any Materials that can furnish out an innocent Diversion, I shall promise him my best Assistance in the working of them up for a publick Entertainment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that offer hints, surprising stories, accounts of widespread (epidemical) vices, or noteworthy virtues are appropriate; the editor will assist contributors in shaping such material for public entertainment and moral instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club admission: visible quearity or peculiar cast of countenance
rubrics_metrics.description: From the 'Act of Deformity': “That no Person whatsoever shall be admitted without a visible Quearity in his Aspect, or peculiar Cast of Countenance; of which the President and Officers for the time being are to determine, and the President to have the casting Voice.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership requires an observable oddness of appearance as judged by officers; the president holds tie-breaking authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club admission: regard gibbosity or obliquity of figure
rubrics_metrics.description: “That a singular Regard be had, upon Examination, to the Gibbosity of the Gentlemen that offer themselves, as Founders Kinsmen, or to the Obliquity of their Figure, in what sort soever.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical irregularities such as hump-backedness (gibbosity) or crookedness (obliquity) are explicit positive criteria for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club admission: miscalculated nose (length or breadth) qualifies
rubrics_metrics.description: “That if the Quantity of any Man's Nose be eminently miscalculated, whether as to Length or Breadth, he shall have a just Pretence to be elected.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronounced disproportions of the nose are singled out as qualifying defects for membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club tie-breaker: thickest skin preference
rubrics_metrics.description: “Lastly, That if there shall be two or more Competitors for the same Vacancy, caeteris paribus, he that has the thickest Skin to have the Preference.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When candidates are otherwise equal, the one judged to have the thickest skin (tolerant/imperturbable) is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club initiation ritual: entertain with codfish and Æsop speech
rubrics_metrics.description: “Every fresh Member, upon his first Night, is to entertain the Company with a Dish of Codfish, and a Speech in praise of Æsop; whose portraiture they have in full Proportion, or rather Disproportion, over the Chimney.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New members must perform a specified comedic ritual (serve codfish and deliver a panegyric to Æsop) as part of induction and club custom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid forcing translations to fit musical metre at expense of sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of contemporary practice: authors “would often make Words of their own which were entirely foreign to the Meaning of the Passages they pretended to translate; their chief Care being to make the Numbers of the English Verse answer to those of the Italian, that both of them might go to the same Tune.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting foreign operas/melodies, translators and adapters should preserve the original meaning and not invent words merely to match syllabic counts or musical measures; priority should be given to semantic fidelity over mechanical rhyme/metric conformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align musical emphasis with semantic importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation: transposition between languages often places 'the finest Notes in the Air' on insignificant words (particles) while leaving important words with weak musical treatment — e.g., soft notes adapted to pity falling on 'Rage' in an English rendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musical setting must respect the semantic weight of words: significant words/ideas should receive prominent musical emphasis, not mere particles like 'and', 'the', 'then'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixed-language performance that breaks dialogue coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: “The King or Hero of the Play generally spoke in Italian, and his Slaves answered him in English... One would have thought it very difficult to have carry'd on Dialogues after this Manner... This was the State of the English Stage for about three Years.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staging where different characters speak/sing in different languages produces incoherent dialogue for the audience; ensure linguistic consistency or provide comprehensible interpretation so dramatic exchange remains intelligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not let music supplant sense or higher dramatic arts
rubrics_metrics.description: “Musick is certainly a very agreeable Entertainment, but if it would take the entire Possession of our Ears, if it would make us incapable of hearing Sense, if it would exclude Arts that have a much greater Tendency to the Refinement of humane Nature: I must confess I would allow it no better Quarter than 'Plato' has done, who banishes it out of his Common-wealth.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism of elevating music above reasoned dramatic content: musical entertainment should not monopolize attention to the detriment of sense, poetry, and other arts that refine human nature; aim for balance.
